test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When very high temperatures are generated inside the cylinder during combustion, what happens to the engine parts?

options.text: They expand and tend to seize.

solution:
The correct answer is __They expand and tend to seize.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• High temperatures during combustion__ can cause significant stress on engine components.
 
• The intense heat makes metal parts expand, reducing the clearances between them.
 
• If the expansion is excessive, the parts may seize or stick, leading to potential engine failure.
 
• Proper cooling systems and materials designed for high heat resistance are essential to prevent thermal damage.
 
• Seizing occurs when thermal expansion exceeds the tolerances in the engine assembly.
 
• Regular maintenance and quality lubricants help mitigate these issues.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Engine Cooling:**

 
 
• Cooling systems use liquids, air, or a combination to dissipate heat generated during combustion.
 
• Effective cooling prevents overheating and reduces the risk of seizing.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Expansion Management:**
 
 
• Engine components are manufactured using metals with known expansion coefficients.
 
• Designs incorporate tolerances to account for thermal expansion.
 
 
 
• **Lubrication:**
 
 
• High-quality lubricants reduce friction and allow smoother movement of components.
 
• They also aid in heat dissipation.
